What is Bardeen?

Browser-based automation tool focused on go-to-market workflows. It runs in your browser using your existing logged-in sessions, which lets it scrape and act on sites (notably LinkedIn) that APIs do not expose, and has pivoted toward AI agents for sales prospecting.

Best for

Automating repetitive browser and LinkedIn-based sales research.

Main features

  • Browser extension automation using your authenticated sessions
  • web scraper builder with no code
  • Magic Box (describe an automation in plain language)
  • AI agents for prospecting, enrichment and outreach
  • playbooks library
  • CRM enrichment and data sync
  • scheduled and triggered runs
  • Bardeen for Sales agent suite.

Practical use cases

  • Scraping a LinkedIn Sales Navigator list into a CRM with enrichment
  • building a prospect list from a directory site
  • auto-logging activity into HubSpot or Salesforce
  • monitoring competitor pages for changes
  • bulk research on a list of companies.

Who is it for?

  • Sales development reps, recruiters, growth marketers, researchers and operations staff doing repetitive browser work.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium with credit-based subscription tiers

Plans described in the source

Free $0 with a limited monthly credit allowance and non-premium actions. Starter around $10-20/mo. Professional around $60-99/mo with higher credits, premium actions and scheduled runs. Business/Enterprise quoted with team management, SSO and dedicated support. Credits are consumed per action, with scraping and AI enrichment costing more. Verify - Bardeen has repositioned around its AI agent offering.

Free plan

Yes - free tier with a monthly credit allowance, adequate for occasional use.

Free trial

Yes - free trials of paid tiers offered.

Usage limits to consider

Credit-metered per action. Premium actions (AI enrichment, large scrapes) consume more credits. Scheduled and background runs are paid-tier only. Browser must be open for many automations unless using cloud runs.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Works on sites with no API by using your own browser session - this is the whole point and nothing else in this list does it as well
  • LinkedIn workflows that would otherwise require paid data vendors
  • very fast to set up with the playbook library
  • genuinely useful free tier.

Limitations to consider

  • Browser-session scraping sits in a legal and terms-of-service grey area, especially on LinkedIn, and accounts have been restricted for aggressive use
  • depends on page structure so automations break when sites change
  • credit pricing is opaque
  • not suitable for server-side or high-reliability automation
  • narrow beyond GTM use cases.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Chrome and Edge browser extensions
  • cloud execution on paid tiers

Languages

  • English interface

API access

Limited - webhooks and Zapier/Make bridges rather than a full public API

Integrations and exports

  • LinkedIn, Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Google Sheets, Airtable, Notion, Slack, Gmail, Outreach, Apollo, Clay, OpenAI

Evaluation notes

Check the terms of service of any site you automate against - LinkedIn in particular actively restricts scraping and account suspension is a real risk. Use conservative rate limits.
